name: OK-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+17
Tom Cole is a well-funded, long-tenured incumbent with a large cash advantage
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97%
Democratic challenger has minimal fundraising and no outside support
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Cole: the district leans Republican by seventeen points, he is a durable incumbent with roughly $2.6 million on hand against a challenger who has raised under $70,000, and markets give the Democrat only a three percent chance. With no competitive polling or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this stays safely Republican.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected national wave shifting Oklahoma swing voters could narrow the margin, though an outright upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tom Cole seeks another term in a southern Oklahoma district that leans Republican by about seventeen points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, roughly $2.6 million on hand, supplemented by outside support, while Democrat Mitchell Jacob has raised about $65,000 and holds minimal cash. An independent candidate also appears on the ballot but lacks visible resources.

No public polling or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Cole. Prediction markets price his chances at about ninety-seven percent. The forecast expects Cole to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
